description: What the shelf window itself may do. Capabilities gate the webview — the least-trusted process here — and nothing else: work done in Rust with an AppHandle is not covered by this file, so a permission listed for the benefit of Rust code grants reach to the webview and buys nothing. Every entry below has a caller in src/, and that is the whole rule. It was not: this listed `core:default`, which is nine permission sets. Two of them mattered rather than merely being untidy. `core:image` allows `from-path` and `rgba` together, which is a file-read primitive that goes around `webview_path` and the asset-protocol scope — the two things the app's confinement rests on — and reaches any decodable image on disk. `core:tray` and `core:menu` let the webview rewrite the tray icon, replace the menus and set the app menu. Neither is used by anything. The whole Tauri JS surface this app touches is `invoke` and `convertFileSrc` (not ACL-gated), `listen`, and `getCurrentWindow().onFocusChanged`, which routes through `listen` — plus `data-tauri-drag-region` in index.html and the drag plugin. Those are the four below. NOT VERIFIED AT RUNTIME: the packaged app has never been launched, so a narrowing that is too tight would show up as a broken webview rather than as a failing gate. See SECURITY.md.
